# Sigyn walks into a home, hearth & real estate firm

Walk into any home, hearth & real estate outfit and watch for ten minutes. You will see a very old act performed with newer props. The act has a name. It is **Sigyn**.

## Before the Office, the Story

**The Wife of Loki.** Snorri names her in the survey of the Æsir with his usual economy: Loki's wife is named Sigyn, and their son is Nari or Narfi.  That is the whole introduction — no father, no hall, no office.  The same catalogue gives Loki his other family: the giantess [[angrboda|Angrboða]], who bore him the wolf [[fenrir|Fenrir]], the World Serpent, and [[hel|Hel]].

**The Captive in the Grove of Kettles.** The seeress of Völuspá, the oldest and greatest poem of the Codex Regius, sees the punishment before it happens: a captive lying under the grove of kettles, something evil-minded in form like Loki — 'and there sits Sigyn, by no means happy about her husband.  Do you understand yet, or what more? 'The stanza is the whole of her eddic portrait, and it is enough: seated, sorrowing, and staying.

### Mental Health & Emotional Wellness

*The wife who endures the dripping venom — steadfast care under unbearable strain.* The match is not poetic license. Strip the trade to its function and the function is the myth.

## Not the First Rebrand

Sigyn's truest kin are inside the corpus itself.  She is the mirror of [[nanna|Nanna]] — the two wives of the Baldr catastrophe, one following her dead husband into the fire, the other staying beside her living one in the pit; devotion answered by death in the one, by endurance without end in the other. The office is only the latest translation.
